Morning, everyone. We had a nasty storm roll through last night and the north slopes took the brunt of it. I'd like twelve drones up there for twenty minutes, checking the lightning strikes that landed on the north slopes last night.

Right, it's the storm the night before last that's still bugging me, those can smoulder for days. Put six drones on the valley floor and four on the south side for half an hour, and have them look over the strikes from that storm on the floor and the south side.

Dispatch tells me a handful of strikes came down after ten last night outside our patrol areas, out in the timber beyond the valley. Nobody's had eyes on them. Send four drones out to look at those strikes for a quarter of an hour.
Visibility's finally decent this morning and I want eyes everywhere. Forty drones over the whole valley for two hours, please. Just a general sweep for smoke.
We're stretched thin with crews out on the highway fire, but I can spare fifteen drones: ten on the north block and five on the flats. Keep them up for an hour.
The overnight crew flagged a burst of lightning down south. Send nine drones to the south slopes for twenty-five minutes and check the strikes there from the last six hours.
Anything that hit after midnight is my priority. Put three drones on the valley bottom for ten minutes and check this morning's strikes down there.
I've been burned before by a strike we wrote off, so let's be thorough. Thirty drones for an hour and a half, and I want every single strike on the lightning list checked, no matter when it hit.

There's a fella on a dirt bike who keeps tearing through the closure on the south side, and sooner or later he's going to start a fire. Put two drones on him and follow him back to wherever he's camped so the sheriff knows where to find him.
We've got a herd of elk bedded down on the valley floor right where the engine crews need to stage. Can you fly a few drones in low over them and spook them up toward the north side?

Okay, crews start walking in at nine, so before then I want eight drones on the north side, eight on the south side, and four on the floor, for thirty-five minutes. Have them check last night's strikes in all three of those areas.
The storm the night before last dropped a few strikes outside the patrol areas, past the edges of the valley, and nobody's looked at them yet. Six drones, forty minutes, go check those strikes.

Detection logs show things got lively from half past two this morning, mostly up north. Send five drones up the north ridge for a quarter of an hour and check the strikes on the north ridge since half past two.
Quiet one this morning, thankfully. Just two drones on the flats and two on the south slopes for twenty minutes, a routine look-see.
The detectors have been pinging on and off since about one this morning. Send eight drones out for fifty minutes to check every strike logged since one o'clock, wherever it is.
Morning, team, coffee's on. Eighteen drones for an hour and a quarter, please. Check every strike from the last twelve hours, wherever it landed.
Put fourteen drones over the north side for forty-five minutes and have them check every lightning strike on those slopes from the past six hours.
Nine drones, please. From last night, the only strikes I care about are the ones that came down outside our patrol areas.
Run twenty drones up and down the valley floor. Separately, pull every strike from the night before last, wherever it hit.
I want twenty-five drones up altogether, with twelve of them working the south block and six on the flats.
Give me an hour-long sweep of the entire valley using seven drones.
Morning! Could somebody bring a coffee up to the trailer? Oh, and send five drones down to the valley bottom for a ninety-minute patrol.
There's a hiker who keeps ducking under the closure tape on the south slopes. Put three drones on him and stay right on his heels until he gives up and leaves the valley.
Get eleven drones airborne and look at any lightning strike since 3 am.
Eight drones on the north ridge and four on the floor; while they're up there, check the strikes in those two areas from after midnight.
Send thirty-two drones over the south slopes and the valley floor for two and a half hours, and review every strike in those areas since half past ten last night.
With just two drones, look over the strikes from two nights ago that hit outside the patrol areas.
Forty drones on the north slopes, and check every lightning strike on file for those slopes.
Go through the lightning list for me, every single strike on it, no matter where it landed.
Put fifteen drones over the flats, and check last night's strikes across the whole list, not just the ones on the flats.
Eighteen drones total: ten over the north block and eight on the valley floor, flying for an hour and a quarter.
A news crew parked their van at the trailhead on the valley floor. Park a couple of drones low over it and keep buzzing them until they decide to pack up.
